name: app/tier-status
title: TierStatus
summary: Where an account stands in the Bundu trust model (assurance.py): the current assurance level, the attestations held beside it as separate chips, the five levels as an ordered list with each level's state in words, the facts held, and what the next level needs with a link to submit evidence. Community is an attestation, never a rung below otp. It takes data and computes no access decision.

props.name: assurance
props.description: The current assurance level (nyuchi/nyuchi-api `gateway/lib/assurance.py`), ordered 0–4. Takes precedence over `tier`. With neither, the level is `none`.

props.name: attestationTypes
props.description: The attestations in force beside the level, as type names or the stored records. Revoked and unknown ones are dropped, as `normalize_attestations` does. Each is shown as its own chip in its `--attestation-*` pair.

props.name: tier
props.description: Legacy: a `bundu.verificationTier` code, read into the model when `assurance` is not set, as assurance.py's fallback does. `community` becomes level `none` plus a community chip, never a rung.

props.name: attestations
props.description: Facts the account holds, in words ("Business registration checked"), with an optional detail (where or when).

props.name: requirements
props.description: What the next rung needs, in words, as the server decided it.

props.name: action
props.description: A link to submit evidence for the next rung.

props.name: levelLabels
props.description: Rename levels in the app's words or another language.

props.name: attestationLabels
props.description: Rename attestations in the app's words or another language.

props.name: tierLabels
props.description: Legacy: rename by tier code. `unverified`, `otp`, `government` and `licensed` name their levels; `community` names the community chip. `levelLabels` and `attestationLabels` win.

props.name: copy
props.type: { current?: string; ladder?: string; attested?: string; held?: string; none?: string; next?: string; top?: string; done?: string; here?: string; upcoming?: string }
props.description: The panel's other words, for another language: "Current level:", the ladder's name, the chips' name ("Attestations"), "What you hold", "No attestations yet.", "Next:", "This is the highest level.", and the rung states "Done", "Current", "Next".

props.name: id
props.description: The id the heading (`<id>-title`) is built from.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: The heading's level; the two sections take the next level.

props.name: class
props.description: Extra classes on the root, merged last.

behaviour: A <section> labelled by its heading, carrying `data-assurance` (the level) and `data-tier` (its legacy projection, `legacy_tier()`). Beside the heading, the level's glyph on its --assurance-* container pair (decorative), and "Current level: <name>" in the level's text colour.

The attestations in force are a named <ul> of chips under the current level, one per attestation (Community Vouched, Registered Business, Domain Verified), each its glyph and its name on its --attestation-* container pair. They carry no rank and are never placed on the ladder.

The ladder is an <ol> of the five assurance levels, lowest first (Unverified, Contact Verified, Documents Checked, Government Verified, Licensed Professional), each with its rank (decorative), its name, and its state in words: "Done" below the current level, "Current" on it (aria-current="step", a muted fill), "Next" on the one above, nothing further up. Reached levels wear their --assurance-* container pair; the others an outline.
"What you hold" lists the facts held with a check glyph, or says "No attestations yet.".
"Next: <name>" lists `requirements` and, with `action`, a link to submit evidence. At the top level it says "This is the highest level." instead.
It computes no access decision and no score: the level, the attestations and the requirements are given by the server (nyuchi-api `assurance.py` decides access).

default.description: A business at Contact Verified with its domain attested, working towards Documents Checked.

requirements: A utility bill in the business's name

unverified.description: No rung reached and nothing held.

localised.description: Every word replaced; the legacy community tier is read as level none plus the community chip.

community.description: Legacy tier community: no level proven, the community attestation as a chip, and no community rung on the ladder.

tuckshop.description: A tuck shop: Contact Verified and vouched for by its street. Neither ranks above the other.

firm.description: A registered firm at Government Verified with business and domain attestations; a revoked community record is dropped.

documented.description: Documents Checked, the level that sits between Contact Verified and Government Verified.

keyboard: The evidence link, when there is one.
aria: The ladder is named ("Verification levels") and so are the chips ("Attestations").
Glyphs and ranks are aria-hidden; every state and every attestation is also written.

theming.brandOverlay: The evidence link is the shell's primary action (`--app-accent`, else `--primary`). Levels and attestations are their --assurance-* / --attestation-* roles in every brand (the legacy --tier-* roles alias them).

responsive: Fills its container; rung names wrap rather than push their state out.
contract:
contract
  slot is "tier-status"
  when default shows strong "Contact Verified"
  when default shows h2 "Verification"
  when default shows h3 "Next: Documents Checked"
  when default shows a "Submit documents"
  when default shows li "Domain Verified"
  when unverified shows h3 "Verification"
  when top shows p "This is the highest level."
  when localised shows strong "Haijathibitishwa"
  when localised shows li "Imethibitishwa na jamii"
  when community shows strong "Unverified"
  when community shows li "Community Vouched"
  when tuckshop shows li "Community Vouched"
  when firm shows li "Registered Business"
  when documented shows strong "Papers checked"
end

checks.say: The panel is a section labelled by its heading, with the level and its legacy projection.
The ladder is an ordered list of the five assurance levels, named.
Community is never a rung.
The current level is marked as the current step.
Each level's state is written: one done, one current, one next.
Levels below are written Done.
The level above is written Next.
A reached level wears its --assurance-* container pair.
A level not reached is an outline.
The current level's glyph is on its container pair.
The current level's name is in its text colour.
Attestations are chips, named, beside the level.
An attestation chip wears its --attestation-* pair and glyph.
The facts held are listed.
Requirements for the next level are listed.
The evidence link.
Nothing held says so.
No attestation, no chips.
Unverified has no level reached: one current, one next, none done.
Unverified shows the shield on the neutral pair.
headingLevel 3 puts the sections at h4.
At the top there is no next level and no link.
Rung states can be renamed.
The next level can be renamed by its legacy tier code.
The chips' name can be replaced.
Legacy community is level none, current, with the community chip.
Legacy community shows the community chip in terracotta's pair.
A tuck shop is Contact Verified with the community chip; otp is the current level.
Revoked and repeated attestations are dropped: business and domain, once each.
Chips keep the order given.
Government is current; three levels below are done.
Documents Checked wears sodalite's role and the file glyph.
Attestations can be renamed.
No script.
